random_seed: none: deterministic exact 2^N state enumeration and convex MaxEnt fits; no RNG used

outputs.metric: test_A.explained_entropy_max_abs_deviation_bits (max deviation of pairwise explained entropy S1-S2 across the coskewness sweep, sign change included)
outputs.tolerance: exact: explained entropy is a function of first and second moments only, held fixed across the sweep

outputs.metric: test_A.true_entropy_swing_bits (range of the TRUE entropy S_N over the same coskewness sweep)
outputs.tolerance: exact enumeration; coskewness moves S_N (and the residual S2-S_N) while S1-S2 stays fixed

outputs.metric: test_B.hof_max (largest higher-order entropy fraction 1-capt across p_obs 0.30..0.005 in the dichotomized-Gaussian family)
outputs.tolerance: exact enumeration; bounded well below 1, monotone but saturating

outputs.metric: test_B.capt_min (smallest fraction of multi-information captured by the pairwise model at p_obs=0.005)
outputs.tolerance: exact enumeration; stays >0.94 down to p_obs~0.005

known_limitations: Exact computation, but on small synthetic ensembles, not neural recordings. TEST A is an exact 3-spin enumeration: it establishes the definitional point (the pairwise MaxEnt explained entropy S1-S2 is a function of first and second moments only, so coskewness cannot enter it) and is exhaustive for that point. TEST B is a finite-N (N=5) equicorrelated dichotomized-Gaussian sparse family with latent correlation rho=0.30; it shows the higher-order entropy fraction stays bounded (<0.06) down to p_obs~0.005 rather than rising to 1, the falsifier the thesis itself requested, but it does not enumerate every biologically plausible sparse model (e.g. heavy-tailed shared-gain families with genuine tail dependence may move HOF higher, though never into S1-S2). The MaxEnt fits are L-BFGS-B on the convex dual; deep-sparse points beyond p_obs~0.005 were excluded because orthant probabilities and the optimiser become numerically fragile there (the duel transcript saw exactly such breakage at p~1e-5).
